questions.question: Q: What are the advantages of reflecting telescopes over refracting?

points.text: Reflectors: no chromatic aberration, easier to make large mirrors (no internal defects), mirrors can be supported from behind, and are cheaper for the same aperture.
Magnification = focal length of objective ÷ focal length of eyepiece.

questions.question: Q: Why are radio telescopes often very large?

points.text: Radio wavelengths are much longer than visible light, so larger dishes are needed to achieve similar resolving power (resolution ∝ aperture/wavelength).

questions.question: Q: Name two advantages of space telescopes.

points.text: 1) No atmospheric distortion (twinkling/scintillation), giving sharper images. 2) Can observe wavelengths blocked by the atmosphere (UV, X-ray, infrared).

questions.question: Q: Describe the difference between alt-az and equatorial mountings.

points.text: Alt-az mounts move in altitude and azimuth (up-down and left-right). Equatorial mounts align one axis with Earth's rotation axis, allowing tracking by rotating one axis at a constant rate.
